game.title: KidnAPPed
store.blurb: A 13-screen rescue thriller. Three phones, one story, one hour.
coupon.soon: Coming soon — coupons for your next game!
lose.title: Oops… not quite
lose.body: That's not it. Talk it over with your team and try again.
win.title: Correct!
s1.s: And somehow, this is now your problem.
s1.b:
{victimName}'s workspace is trashed. {victimName} is gone. And judging by the scene, we're looking at a kidnapping. Or an escape. Or the most aggressive work-from-home transition in corporate history.
We checked to see who was available to help.
Bad news: it's you.
So fire up those brain cells, attempt something resembling teamwork, and go find {victimName}.
This should go great.
s2.g12.s: Which is mildly concerning, but here we are.
s2.g12.b:
You're looking at an image from {victimName}'s computer. Somewhere in there is something your team needs to move forward.
Zoom in. Scan everything. Question every pixel. Look for anything suspicious, weird, or just slightly off.
Found something? Great. You can't type it anywhere.
You'll have to explain it to your teammates. Yes, actual human communication. Godspeed.
s2.g3.b:
The other two got a look at {victimName}'s computer. You got the keyboard.
Power. Responsibility. A text box.
The password is five letters in English, and the answer is hiding somewhere in what they can see.
So compare notes, overthink everything, argue confidently about who's wrong, and enter the password here.
Stuck? There are hints. We won't judge. Much.
s3.s: Folders. Files. And one video we absolutely did not need in our lives.
s3.b:
Good news: we found the ransom note.
Bad news: the kidnappers want a million dollars and a video of the boss dancing to “Baby Shark.”
Honestly, the million feels reasonable now.
Anyway, there's also a creepy video. Maybe it'll help us find {victimName}. Maybe it'll just permanently alter your YouTube recommendations.
Only one way to find out. Hit Play.
s4.g1.s: And congratulations — figuring out what the hell you just watched is your job.
s4.g1.b:
You've got the video. Watch carefully. Something in there is supposed to lead you to the answer.
Notice everything. Replay it. Freeze-frame it. Become the kind of person who says, “Wait, go back three seconds.”
When you think you've cracked it, enter the answer here.
No pressure. {victimName} is missing while you're on Replay #6.
s4.g2.s: Yep. Hands. That's where we are now.
s4.g2.b:
The image in front of you is part of the solution. Look carefully, compare it with what the others received, and try to figure out what these hands are trying to say.
And hey, hey — not everyone here is a programmer. What exactly does that mean?
s4.g3.s: Different hands. Because apparently consistency was out of scope.
s4.g3.b:
There's a reason your image isn't identical to everyone else's.
Study the details. Tell the others exactly what you see. Compare everything. Somewhere in this mess, the pieces connect.
Alexander the Great. Depth. For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
s5.s: Apparently there are easier ways to share a password.
s5.b:
Those people in the video did not exactly scream “fun coworkers to grab drinks with.”
But message received. You now have the password to {victimName}'s social media.
So naturally, we're logging in. Maybe his posts contain a clue. Maybe you're about to learn why {victimName} should never have been allowed online.
Either way: start scrolling.
s6.g13.s: Privacy left the chat several puzzles ago.
s6.g13.b:
You've got a collection of {victimName}'s social posts. They're all about chocolate. Because obviously, when someone disappears under suspicious circumstances, the investigation eventually leads to dessert content.
Look carefully. Likes. Platforms. Posts. Details.
We promise this isn't about the recipe.
s6.g2.s: While everyone else gets social media. HR has been notified.
s6.g2.b:
Find your way out and pay attention to what you discover along the way.
You're also the one with the answer box, so communication with the others is going to be fairly important.
Without them, you're basically just staring at a maze with confidence.
m.h1: What's the name of the maze? What are the others looking for on social media? What appears in every post?
m.h2: Solve the maze, then connect the… in order.
s7.t: Wait… is that a phone number?
s7.b:
Put all those digits together and — boom — you've got a phone number.
Progress. Probably.
Now, what do responsible adults do when they find a mysterious phone number during a kidnapping investigation?
Absolutely not what you're about to do.
Call it.
s8.g12.t: Nope. We did not need to hear that.
s8.g12.s: If creepy voicemail were an Olympic event, we'd be looking at a medal contender.
s8.g12.b:
We could stop here. Tell everyone we gave it our best shot. Send {victimName} a DoorDash gift card. Maybe put on Netflix and pretend none of this happened.
Tempting. But no.
Listen again. There's something hidden in that message, and unfortunately, you're now emotionally invested.
s8.g3.s: Trust us. Huge win for you.
s8.g3.b:
The others just listened to a voicemail they'll probably discuss in therapy someday. You got a text box.
Listen to your teammates. Figure out what they heard. Enter the answer here.
And if they suggest abandoning the mission and ordering tacos instead… they have a case.
a.h1: We're looking for three digits. Any ideas?
a.h2: This isn't really a trip, is it? Maybe open a map and follow the lines.
s9.s: Because entering suspicious buildings is apparently part of the roadmap now.
s9.b:
The number you found appears on the map from the first room. We plugged it into your navigation systems, and congratulations: you have a destination.
When you get there, you'll find several doors.
Which one should you open?
No clue. That feels like a you problem.
s10.t: Great. You picked the first door.
s10.s: Bold strategy. Or you just started on the left.
s10.b:
Inside: chaos. Very on-brand for this investigation.
But something's off. You're not all seeing exactly the same thing.
Compare your images. Look carefully. Find what doesn't match.
p.h1: Spot the difference. Something is different between the images. Come on, we believe in you.
p.h2: Player 2 is the odd one out. What can they see that the others can't?
s11.s: Or we've become extremely efficient at making bad decisions.
s11.b:
We found an envelope with a guitar on it. Sure. Why not.
At this point, a guitar is probably one of the more reasonable things we've encountered.
There's a tiny message next to it: “Follow my point of view.”
Creepy. We're in.
Open it.
s12.g12.s: Because apparently words were too user-friendly.
s12.g12.b:
You've got a collection of images covered in strange symbols. Someone, somewhere, clearly believed you'd know what to do with these.
We admire their confidence.
Look closely. Compare what you have. Talk to each other.
There's logic here. Probably.
s12.g3.s: Banknotes so fake Monopoly's legal team is getting nervous.
s12.g3.b:
You've got a collection of extremely questionable-looking banknotes. But don't rush — you don't have the whole puzzle yet.
Something else is coming, and when it does, you'll need to connect it with what you've figured out here.
So inspect the money. Remember what matters. And wait.
Yes, waiting is technically part of the puzzle now.
f.h1: Remember when we were told, “Follow my point of view”? What could that mean?
f.h2: We have an email address, right? Let's send it an email. We'll probably get a reply. But knowing this game, the reply will probably lead to something else. Starting to recognize the tune yet?
s13.s: No, that's not what you played. We're just extremely happy this is over.
s13.b:
You played together. You cracked the final puzzle. And {victimName} is back.
After everything that just happened, we're honestly not sure who needs a recovery day more — {victimName} or you.
But that sounds like tomorrow's problem.
For now? Let the chaos begin.
popup.skippedBody: Moving on — no points for this one.
s2.h1: Who is Dvořák? Is there another famous Dvořák besides the 19th-century Czech composer?
s2.h2: There is a keyboard layout called Dvorak. You can look it up using an image or an online tool. How would you type VANDA?
s4.h1: Play the video and tell your teammates what you see. It's not the answer, but it's an important part of getting there.
s4.h2: What do those initials stand for? What do Player 3's clues have in common? What keeps repeating in each one? Connect the dots and you'll get there.
